- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥1.0) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 2–5% relative to model output.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-1.0), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% to align with downward momentum.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in subsequent days; apply a 1–3 day decay filter to smooth out overreaction.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive within 3–5 days, model often fails to adjust quickly; delay forecast adjustment until sentiment stabilizes or exceeds 0.75.
- Mean reversion is strong in 3–5 day horizons; if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to ignore sentiment shifts >2 days old; if sentiment changes >1.0 in last 3 days, adjust forecast to reflect new sentiment direction.
